You've probably seen YouTube thumbnails with massive futuristic interfaces covering someone's entire vision.
And you've probably watched a demo and thought: hang on, how much of that is actually in the glasses?

脚本原文: What you actually see
First, the bit the thumbnails keep getting creative with.
You're getting green text and graphics in a defined display area, through both lenses. The interface doesn't fill your entire vision.
The G2 uses a binocular waveguide system, which is different from the original Halliday display. So older footage won't necessarily show you what this pair looks like.
It's built around things like messages, notes and information you can glance at. Think checking something quickly, then getting on with what you were doing.
The idea makes sense. But the display needs to be readable without constantly adjusting the glasses or struggling to find the right position.
And you know what? These haven't been half bad.

The display is definitely one of the less obstructive ones that I've tried, the balance between the interface, and the real world is quite nicely done, the green edges aren't too thick, they're just about readable enough, without completely compromising your view and focus.
不符合原因: 这句是显示实测的收口：第 9–16 句都在讲显示（不碍眼、绿字边界勉强可读），但品牌方列为硬件优势的“高亮度”整片一次都没讲到，观众看不到白天、窗边这类强光下还能不能看清。属于核心目的 ③（卖点介绍到位：没讲到）。
修改意见: 建议补一句亮度实测，讲清白天、窗边这类强光下屏幕还能不能看清；不建议引用具体亮度数值。

脚本原文: And what I really like is it doesn't feel like everything is inside a box.
What these don't have, is a camera. So there's no recording video, taking photos, or asking the glasses to read a menu you're looking at.
If that's what you wanted, that's already a reason to choose something else.
But I'm personally completely split, I hate walking around with a camera on my face, but, I can't deny it extends the functionality of the glasses significantly.
What you hear
What they do have is open-ear audio.
Music, calls and AI responses can come through speakers in the arms, so a quick call doesn't necessarily mean digging out your earbuds.
You also get to keep your ears physically open, which I can see being handy around the house or walking somewhere.
But speaker quality and sound leakage matter more than the word "immersive" on a marketing slide.
不符合原因: 这句把品牌方描述这项硬件优势用的词“immersive”直接点评成营销话术，等于把“沉浸音质的立体声扬声器”这条要主推的卖点本身否掉了。
品牌方 brief 原文: Stereo speakers with immersive sound quality

脚本原文: But I would describe these as immersive, just not in the same way as a dolby atmos setup might be, despite sound leakage, they really have to be quite loud for someone else to hear them. They feel personal, fit for purpose, and yeah although I wouldn't swap them for my normal audio device, listening to music is quite pleasant.
But the audio is only one part of how you interact with them.
What the AI actually does
There are two different AI experiences here, and it's worth separating them.
Hold the action button and you can ask Halliday AI a question.
"What is the weather like in bristol from 2pm today"
Works as you'd expect.

脚本原文: Then there's Meeting Flow.

Halliday's idea here is to follow a conversation and bring up useful information while it's happening. That includes recovering the recent discussion, researching an unfamiliar topic, and flagging decisions or unclear commitments.
For example, somebody says, "We'll send that quote next week."
Who's sending it? Which day? Those are the details you want settled before everybody leaves.
That's the useful distinction: help during the conversation, followed by a summary afterwards.

It's something that when I was working in an office, I would have considered gold, the amount of times a meeting ended and I think of a million questions to ask afterwards - I have my own business now, but I have my wedding coming up in a few weeks, and even using the meeting flow feature for that, has been legitimately helpful.
I can see the benefit if you spend a lot of time in meetings, or struggle to keep track of everything that was said.

But a neat summary still needs checking. Names, dates, who agreed to what. And AI answers can be wrong, including about current information. There's a few things that it definitely misheard, that would have been helpful, but, i still think it's doing a far better job than you would on your own.
Translation and captions
Now, Translation is another feature where the benefit is easy to understand.
Someone speaks another language, and translated text appears in your view. You can follow what they're saying without holding your phone between you.
But there's a missing half of the conversation: how do they understand your reply?
Don't assume the phrase "live translation" means both people can just talk normally and everything happens automatically.
Visual translation, in glasses, makes so much sense, arguably way better than earphones on their own, but there is still that barrier there.

Captions deserve attention too. Under another smart-glasses review, a deaf viewer described conversation assistance as putting them back in touch with the world, and in my very first smart glasses review, I made the exact same observation, for people hard of hearing, I mean these are incredible.

I will say though, with these, and other ai glasses, wind can be a huge problem, the microphones really struggle to pick up what's being said, so there's a big environmental factor to consider there, we're not at the point where they can be relied on.
不符合原因: 全片唯一讲麦克风实际表现的这句把整体结论写成“目前还不能依赖”，品牌方列为硬件优势的“4 个麦克风组成的更好声学腔体”没有讲出来，观众只看到缺点、看不到这项硬件在安静场景下的表现。属于核心目的 ③（卖点介绍到位：讲反）。
修改意见: 需调整表述，不能说整片结论是“还不能依赖”。建议将口径改为户外风噪下受限、室内通话可用，并注意保持客观。

脚本原文: The actual cost
Now for Money.
The listed price is 599 US dollars before offers. And the meeting features use credits.
Halliday's launch membership page includes a year of Basic, with around four hours of full Meeting Flow per month. Summary-only use has a different allowance.
Everyday AI, live translation and daily functions are listed as unlimited. So the whole pair doesn't become useless because you've used your meeting allowance.
Four hours of meeting assistance isn't much if you're in meetings every day. For the average employee, you might get away with that.
But check the price of the plan you'll actually need, including what happens after any introductory offer ends.

"Included for a year" and "included forever" are very different things. I'm not going to complain about having a subscription on these though, and i usually would, but I just completely understand that AI compute is not free.

Being completely honest and upfront though, there is a big longevity question mark here for me - When Samsung come out with their glasses, they will almost certainly draw from your gemini pro subscription, which instantly would make me think twice about purchasing a subscription from halliday.
不符合原因: Gemini 与 ChatGPT 在这句里只跟订阅成本与长期可用性的顾虑绑在一起，品牌方列为硬件优势的“由 Gemini 与 ChatGPT 驱动的更强算力”整片没有讲出来。属于核心目的 ③（卖点介绍到位：没讲到）。
品牌方 brief 原文: Stronger computing power powered by Gemini & ChatGPT
修改意见: 建议补一句算力实测，讲清连续追问时的响应速度、对话上下文能不能延续；不建议引用具体数值。

脚本原文: I think companies like this, need to work on relationships with the frontier ai companies, so that people's everyday ai subscriptions can be made use of, rather than having to pay for a subscription on top.
Privacy
But now for a note on privacy.
Some people actively want glasses without a camera. They want the assistance without pointing a lens at everyone they meet.
Fair enough. But these still have microphones.
Halliday says conversation context stays on your device and describes protections around AI training. That statement alone doesn't tell us that every AI task is processed locally.
What gets captured, what gets sent away, and what gets retained are separate questions. If those details aren't clear, I wouldn't give you a blanket "it's all private".
And again, to be clear, you also can't currently connect your own external AI model. Your existing ChatGPT subscription or local server isn't something you can just plug into these.
Actually wearing them
Now, would you actually want them on your face all day?
They're listed at 49 grams, but comfort isn't just a number. The fit behind your ears, pressure on your nose and alignment of the display all matter, I speak from experience.
I've found them to be some of the more comfortable glasses, the nose pads in particular are more sensible than other glasses I've tried.
Comfort aside, there's a touch bar and an action button for controlling them.
That's the interaction you'll actually be doing. It needs to feel convenient enough that you keep using it.
Battery has an important qualification too. Halliday quotes twelve hours of regular use, or up to three hours of intensive use.
不符合原因: 这句只讲了续航时长，品牌方列为硬件优势的“长续航＋快充”里的快充整片没有讲到。属于核心目的 ③（卖点介绍到位：没讲到）。
修改意见: 建议补一句快充实测，讲清出门前短时补电后当天的可用情况；不建议引用具体数值。

脚本原文: So twelve hours doesn't mean twelve hours of continuous meeting assistance. Judge that against your day, especially if you're buying for captions or long meetings. I went out on a day trip to oxford to test these out and about, and they just about made it through the day at around 8 hours.
Your phone is still involved
Something to consider, is your phone is still part of this. The Halliday app pairs over Bluetooth, with versions for iPhone and Android.
That means phone compatibility and software reliability belong in the buying decision just as much as the display.
There's also a cheatsheet for presentation notes. Having your next talking point in view could be more useful than half the flashy AI demos.
And yes, you can filter your notifications. Every group chat in front of your eyes sounds like a fairly efficient way to ruin your afternoon.
Prescription lenses and returns
If you already wear glasses, there's another thing to check.
Halliday currently supplies the prescription lenses itself, and says progressive and photochromic options aren't supported.

I do wonder if I should have got prescription lenses, I only wear glasses for driving, and sometimes the text for me can be a little blurry, so if you are considering these and think you will be able to play with some settings to get the display right if your eyes aren't perfect, don't assume you can take these to your usual optician or get the same lenses you already wear.
不符合原因: 这句把处方镜片讲成“别指望拿旧镜片、渐进与变色不支持”的限制清单，品牌方列为硬件优势的“处方镜片兼容”没有被正面讲出来，戴眼镜的观众只看到麻烦、看不到可以直接配一副。属于核心目的 ③（卖点介绍到位：讲弱）。
修改意见: 建议先讲处方镜片可以按需配镜、当作日常一副眼镜使用，再讲既有镜片不能移装、渐进与变色选项不支持的客观限制；不建议与同类产品做横向对比。

脚本原文: Returns matter too. Their policy gives eligible non-prescription orders fourteen days. Custom prescription orders are generally final sale unless defective or supplied incorrectly.
That's a fairly important difference if you're spending this much on glasses you haven't tried on.

Which brings me to a final design point, these are really cool glasses, in terms of design, I'm just not a really cool person. As much as I'd love to, I don't think i can pull these off, i kind of look like a wanna be edgy harry potter. Other people will look awesome, but having one style for various different face shapes, is a limiting factor of these glasses.
不符合原因: 全片只有这一句专门讲外观设计，只讲自己适不适合、一种造型适配不了所有脸型，品牌方列为硬件优势的“高级醋酸纤维板材”整片没有讲到，镜框材质与做工这层卖点缺席。属于核心目的 ③（卖点介绍到位：没讲到）。
修改意见: 建议补一句镜框材质与做工的实测，讲清上手的质感、表面处理与铰链手感；不建议与同类产品做横向对比。

脚本原文: The verdict
So, where does that leave us?
I think the appeal is pretty clear: useful information and audio available without constantly reaching for your phone.
If conversation assistance, captions or translation would regularly solve a problem for you, there's a reason to be interested.
But at this price, "that looks cool" wouldn't be enough for me.
The display, audio and AI need to earn their place alongside the fit, battery, software, privacy arrangements and ongoing cost.
And if you need a camera, different prescription lenses, or your own AI setup, those limitations matter. You don't have to talk yourself around them.
A small display can be useful. But don't just buy them because it looks cool, you need to be able to make use of the features to warrant the cost.
不符合原因: 结尾把购买理由收成“别因为好看就买”，只说清了对什么人要谨慎，没有说清这副眼镜适合谁、为什么应该选它。
品牌方 brief 原文: End with who Halliday is for and why they should choose it.
